candidates.locator: Chapter 2.3 — Of God, and of the Holy Trinity
candidates.phrase: the Son is eternally begotten of the Father
candidates.rationale: Directly asserts the eternal filial relation of the Son to the Father as a divine person.
candidates.chunk_text: In the unity of the Godhead there be three persons, of one substance, power, and eternity: God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost: the Father is of none, neither begotten, nor proceeding; the Son is eternally begotten of the Father; the Holy Ghost eternally proceeding from the Father and the Son.

candidates.phrase: The Son of God, the second person in the Trinity, being very and eternal God
candidates.rationale: Names the Son of God as eternal, divine, second Trinitarian person, affirming the eternal Logos identity.
candidates.chunk_text: The Son of God, the second person in the Trinity, being very and eternal God, of one substance and equal with the Father, did, when the fullness of time was come, take upon him man’s nature, with all the essential properties, and common infirmities thereof, yet without sin; being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost, in the womb of the virgin Mary, of her substance. So that two whole, perfect, and distinct natures, the Godhead and the manhood, were inseparably joined together in one person, without conversion, composition, or confusion. Which person is very God, and very man, yet one Christ, the only Mediator between God and man.

candidates.phrase: the Lord Jesus, his only begotten Son, to be the Mediator
candidates.rationale: Asserts God's eternal purpose regarding his only begotten Son, affirming the filial title of the divine Son.
candidates.chunk_text: It pleased God, in his eternal purpose, to choose and ordain the Lord Jesus, his only begotten Son, to be the Mediator between God and man, the Prophet, Priest, and King, the Head and Savior of his church, the Heir of all things, and Judge of the world: unto whom he did from all eternity give a people, to be his seed, and to be by him in time redeemed, called, justified, sanctified, and glorified.

candidates.phrase: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost; and these three are one God
candidates.rationale: Names the Son as a divine person in the Godhead, equal in power and glory with the Father.
candidates.chunk_text: How many persons are there in the Godhead? A. There are three persons in the Godhead; the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost; and these three are one God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory.

candidates.phrase: being the eternal Son of God, became man
candidates.rationale: Explicitly asserts the eternal Sonship of the Logos prior to and distinct from the incarnation.
candidates.chunk_text: Who is the redeemer of God’s elect? A. The only redeemer of God’s elect is the Lord Jesus Christ, who, being the eternal Son of God, became man, and so was, and continueth to be, God and man in two distinct natures, and one person, forever.

candidates.phrase: Christ, the Son of God, became man
candidates.rationale: Affirms Christ as the Son of God who became man, asserting the filial divine identity of the Logos.
candidates.chunk_text: How did Christ, being the Son of God, become man? A. Christ, the Son of God, became man, by taking to himself a true body and a reasonable soul, being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost in the womb of the virgin Mary, and born of her, yet without sin.

candidates.phrase: is the only Son of God— eternally begotten, not made or created
candidates.rationale: Confesses the Son's eternal generation from the Father, asserting the eternal filial relation of the Logos.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe that Jesus Christ, according to his divine nature, is the only Son of God— eternally begotten, not made or created, for then he would be a creature. He is one in essence with the Father; coeternal; the exact image of the person of the Father and the “reflection of God’s glory,” being like the Father in all things. Jesus Christ is the Son of God not only from the time he assumed our nature but from all eternity, as the following testimonies teach us when they are taken together. Moses says that God created the world; and John says that all things were created through the Word, which he calls God. The apostle says that God created the world through the Son. He also says that God created all things through Jesus Christ. And so it must follow that the one who is called God, the Word, the Son, and Jesus Christ already existed before creating all things. Therefore the prophet Micah says that Christ’s origin is “from ancient days.” And the apostle says that the Son has “neither beginning of days nor end of life.” So then, he is the true eternal God, the Almighty, whom we invoke, worship, and serve. 13 ; 14 15 16 17 18 19

candidates.phrase: The Son is the Word, the Wisdom, and the image of the Father.
candidates.rationale: Identifies the Son as the eternal distinct person who is the image of the Father, expressing the eternal filial relation.
candidates.chunk_text: In keeping with this truth and Word of God we believe in one God, who is one single essence, in whom there are three persons, really, truly, and eternally distinct according to their incommunicable properties— namely, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The Father is the cause, origin, and source of all things, visible as well as invisible. The Son is the Word, the Wisdom, and the image of the Father. The Holy Spirit is the eternal power and might, proceeding from the Father and the Son. Nevertheless, this distinction does not divide God into three, since Scripture teaches us that the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit each has a distinct subsistence distinguished by characteristics— yet in such a way that these three persons are only one God. It is evident then that the Father is not the Son and that the Son is not the Father, and that likewise the Holy Spirit is neither the Father nor the Son. Nevertheless, these persons, thus distinct, are neither divided nor fused or mixed together. For the Father did not take on flesh, nor did the Spirit, but only the Son. The Father was never without the Son, nor without the Holy Spirit, since all these are equal from eternity, in one and the same essence. There is neither a first nor a last, for all three are one in truth and power, in goodness and mercy.

survivors.phrase: Christ alone is the eternal, natural Son of God
survivors.rationale: Directly asserts that the eternal, natural Sonship belongs uniquely to Christ as the divine Logos.
survivors.chunk_text: Q. Why is he called God’s “only begotten Son” when we also are God’s children? A. Because Christ alone is the eternal, natural Son of God. We, however, are adopted children of God— adopted by grace through Christ.

survivors.phrase: is the only Son of God— eternally begotten, not made or created
survivors.rationale: Confesses the Son's eternal generation from the Father, asserting the eternal filial relation of the Logos.
survivors.chunk_text: We believe that Jesus Christ, according to his divine nature, is the only Son of God— eternally begotten, not made or created, for then he would be a creature. He is one in essence with the Father; coeternal; the exact image of the person of the Father and the “reflection of God’s glory,” being like the Father in all things. Jesus Christ is the Son of God not only from the time he assumed our nature but from all eternity, as the following testimonies teach us when they are taken together. Moses says that God created the world; and John says that all things were created through the Word, which he calls God. The apostle says that God created the world through the Son. He also says that God created all things through Jesus Christ. And so it must follow that the one who is called God, the Word, the Son, and Jesus Christ already existed before creating all things. Therefore the prophet Micah says that Christ’s origin is “from ancient days.” And the apostle says that the Son has “neither beginning of days nor end of life.” So then, he is the true eternal God, the Almighty, whom we invoke, worship, and serve. 13 ; 14 15 16 17 18 19

survivors.phrase: The Son of God, the second person in the Trinity, being very and eternal God
survivors.rationale: Names the Son of God as eternal, divine, second Trinitarian person, affirming the eternal Logos identity.
survivors.chunk_text: The Son of God, the second person in the Trinity, being very and eternal God, of one substance and equal with the Father, did, when the fullness of time was come, take upon him man’s nature, with all the essential properties, and common infirmities thereof, yet without sin; being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost, in the womb of the virgin Mary, of her substance. So that two whole, perfect, and distinct natures, the Godhead and the manhood, were inseparably joined together in one person, without conversion, composition, or confusion. Which person is very God, and very man, yet one Christ, the only Mediator between God and man.

survivors.chunk_text: Who is the redeemer of God’s elect? A. The only redeemer of God’s elect is the Lord Jesus Christ, who, being the eternal Son of God, became man, and so was, and continueth to be, God and man in two distinct natures, and one person, forever.

survivors.phrase: being from all eternity the Son of God, in the bosom of the Father

survivors.chunk_text: How did Christ humble himself in his conception and birth? A. Christ humbled himself in his conception and birth, in that, being from all eternity the Son of God, in the bosom of the Father, he was pleased in the fullness of time to become the son of man, made of a woman of low estate, and to be born of her; with divers circumstances of more than ordinary abasement.
